target.title: fix(cron): channel failure alerts drop when global webhook failure destination is set
target.body:
Closes #102235

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who set a job-level channel failure destination (for example `--failure-channel slack --failure-to #alerts` without `--failure-mode`) would never receive cron failure alerts when `cron.failureDestination` defaulted to a global webhook. The chat target was treated as a webhook URL, failed validation, and the failure notification was dropped with only a "webhook URL is invalid, skipping" log.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveFailureDestination` only reconciled `mode` when the job object included a `mode` field. A channel-shaped job override without `mode` therefore kept the inherited global webhook mode. This change treats a channel-shaped job failure destination without `mode` as announce (matching primary delivery defaults), clears an inherited webhook URL when mode switches, and leaves to-only overrides free to inherit a global webhook mode.

Proof covers the full gateway finished path: real Gateway process + `cron.add` + forced `cron.run` with an isolated agent failure, asserting announce dispatch and no webhook POST of `#alerts`.

## User Impact

Cron failure alerts configured as channel/announce routes keep working even when a global webhook failure destination is also configured. Operators no longer lose job-level Slack/Telegram/etc. failure routes just because they omitted `--failure-mode`.

## Evidence

```text
# Resolver unit regressions
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/delivery.test.ts
 ✓ |cron| src/cron/delivery.test.ts (22 tests)

# Gateway notification unit path
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-cron-notifications.test.ts -t "#102235"
 ✓ announces channel-shaped failure destinations without mode under a global webhook default (#102235)

# Real Gateway + cron.run force (integration)
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts -t "#102235"
 ✓ announces channel-shaped failure destinations without mode under a global webhook default (#102235)  1114ms
 Tests  1 passed | 20 skipped
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Job-level channel-shaped failure destinations without `mode` must not inherit a global webhook mode and silently drop channel failure alerts after a real cron failure finishes.
- Environment: macOS local checkout; real Gateway via `startServerWithClient` in `src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts`; branch `grok/cron-failure-dest-channel-mode` at `42e6bc1a8bf678180450af75d8a9d1769f8650bc`.
- Current-main contrast:
  - Inputs: config `cron.failureDestination = { mode: "webhook", to: "https://hook.example/cron" }`; job `delivery.failureDestination = { channel: "slack", to: "#alerts" }` (no mode); isolated agent run returns error; `cron.run` force.
  - Main: resolver keeps `mode: "webhook"` + `to: "#alerts"` → gateway logs `cron: failure destination webhook URL is invalid, skipping` → alert dropped.
  - This branch: Gateway finishes the failed job, then calls `sendFailureNotificationAnnounce` for Slack `#alerts` and does not POST `#alerts` as a webhook.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.cron.test.ts -t "#102235"`
  2. Test boots a real Gateway, writes the global webhook failureDestination into config, `cron.add`s the channel-shaped job, forces a failed isolated run, and asserts the finished-notification path.
- Evidence after fix (Gateway runtime transcript from the integration test):
  ```text
  Gateway startServerWithClient()
  writeCronConfig({ cron: { failureDestination: { mode: "webhook", to: "https://hook.example/cron" } } })
  cron.add name="channel fd no mode"
    delivery: { mode: "none", failureDestination: { channel: "slack", to: "#alerts" } }  // no mode
  isolated agent returns status=error
  cron.run { id, mode: "force" } → finished event

  Observed on this branch:
  - sendFailureNotificationAnnounce called once
  - target: { channel: "slack", to: "#alerts", inheritSessionThread: false }
  - message: '⚠️ Cron job "channel fd no mode" failed: unknown error'
  - fetchWithSsrFGuard not called (no webhook POST of #alerts / no invalid-URL webhook path)

  Terminal:
  ✓ announces channel-shaped failure destinations without mode under a global webhook default (#102235)  1114ms
  Tests  1 passed | 20 skipped
  ```
- Control check:
  - Resolver still inherits global webhook for a to-only override without channel/mode.
  - Existing gateway webhook failureDestination cases still post to real webhook URLs when mode is explicitly webhook.
- Observed result after fix: a forced failed cron job on a real Gateway dispatches the channel-shaped failure destination as announce to Slack `#alerts` instead of treating it as an invalid webhook URL under the global webhook default.
- What was not tested: live Slack/Telegram tenant network delivery of the announce payload (channel transport is mocked at the announce helper boundary, same as other gateway cron failure announce tests); full remote Crabbox `pnpm check:changed` in this contributor environment.

## AI disclosure

This fix was implemented with AI assistance (Grok). The behavior change and tests were verified locally against the reported resolver path and a real Gateway forced cron failure path; please review the inheritance edge cases and compatibility semantics before merge.
